support_floor.reason: Zero-support floor: a row in one of the floor's scopes (the UC payment-distribution and benefit-cap amount bands, the HMRC SPI income bands by total income and SPI Table 3.10's self-employment income bands, and the band-H council-tax rows by English region) whose compiled matrix row reaches no source household (household_source_id) with a positive prior weight cannot be fitted by any weights (the solver's initialiser refuses a nonzero target with no support), so it is dropped from the solve, not pooled. A row that some households carry stays bound however few they are; when fewer than 10 distinct source households carry it, its model figures are withheld from every written surface (the UK Data Service working floor, CD171 section 5.2.1). Each scope holds one unit, because its share ceiling sums published values. The floor's receipt reports each target's dropped published total and each scope's dropped share, and the run refuses when a scope's drops pass either of its ceilings or when a per-row exclusion names a row the floor drops.
support_floor.adjudication: microcosm#1095 U3, ruled 2026-10-16 with the fifth ports PR (floor 10) and revised 2026-10-21 with #1333: a cell that rests on fewer than 10 records is no reason to leave a row out, only a measured distortion of the calibration is. The floor drops only rows no household carries, the benefit-cap amount bands join its scope and their per-row entries retire, and the figures of rows under 10 source households are withheld, as the BRMA rows' are (under three since María's ruling of 2026-10-29). The thirteen entries it retired (the eleven benefit-cap amount bands and the two HMRC £500k to £1m cells) and the A/B that retired them: experiments/1095-uk-thin-row-binding-receipts.md. Extended on 2026-10-22 (María's ruling on the next policyengine-uk bump) to the HMRC SPI income-band families and the band-H council-tax rows by region, in scopes of one unit each with their own ceilings. On #1333's policyengine-uk 2.145.0 spine every HMRC £1m-and-over cell and every band-H region cell has carriers. The three band-H region entries retire and their rows bind, with their figures withheld where fewer than 10 source households carry them (fewer than three since María's ruling of 2026-10-29, receipt_counts.UK_DISCLOSURE_FLOOR); the ten HMRC £1m-and-over cells, bound on arm 1, distorted their neighbours and stay held on that measurement, so the HMRC scopes cover the bands below them. Extended on 2026-10-29 in microcosm#1420, in answer to the independent review's finding 7 and pending María's confirmation, to the SPI families microcosm#1418 binds, Table 3.7's other income by total-income band and Table 3.10's self-employment bands from GBP 1 to GBP 10,000: a row of theirs that no household carries is dropped and receipted as its siblings' rows are, not refused. The ceilings are unchanged, so the HMRC amounts scope's 2-row cap, signed for seven families, now covers nine, and the counts scope's, signed for seven, now covers eight; María confirms or re-sizes them (the re-reviews of microcosm#1420, H and 4).

exclusions.name: ons.savings_interest_income
exclusions.reason: Concept, not a weight question: the ONS UKEA HAXV row is households' (S.14) D.41 interest resources in the national accounts (FISIM-adjusted, including the unincorporated-business part of the sector; GBP 95.5bn at 2025) while the model's savings_interest_income is cash interest, so the row is unreachable by design (-82 percent on the v20 national candidate). From 2026-09-22 the fitting anchor for interest is the SPI 2023-24 Table 3.7 interest rows by total-income band, uprated to the calibration year (hmrc.spi.savings_interest_income.*, PolicyEngine/chronicle#280 lane); this row is measured on every evaluation as the D.41 diagnostic and never fitted. Retire only with a declared D.41-to-cash bridge.
exclusions.adjudication: PolicyEngine/microcosm#1006 (issue comment 5812206367, the register rulings María gave in session: ruling R3 of 2026-09-22, the SPI interest rows bound and the ONS row a measured diagnostic; income-anchor lane, PolicyEngine/chronicle#280); previously microcosm#762 A16 (2026-09-03); renewed on 2026-10-16 to 2027-01-08 by juaristi22 in session (folded into the sixth microcosm#1095 ports PR): the gap is one of concept, not of weights, so the row stays a measured diagnostic until a D.41-to-cash bridge is declared.

exclusions.name: obr.housing_benefit
exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16 (spine-q design weights unless stated). FRS 2024-25 reports 1.56m Housing Benefit benefit units, 99.9 percent renters, near the DWP GB caseload (1.94m in January 2025 falling to 1.46m by December); the spine carries 1.21m GB reporters (GBP 7.15bn reported) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households without tenure coherence: 363k of its 449k reporting units sit in owner-occupied households and can never be paid. The engine then pays Housing Benefit only to reporting units with a rented tenure, not drawn into Universal Credit, under the capital limit and carrying the household's rent (rent is the household head's benefit unit's alone; claims_all_entitled_benefits collapses to a scalar, so there is no take-up lever): 407k all-pension-age reporting units were drawn into Universal Credit by the 55 percent take-up draw although they cannot claim it, and the working-age remainder is pared by the means test. On the Q50f candidate the engine pays 235k units and GBP 2.13bn against the OBR GBP 12.10bn (-82 percent); the U8 lever receipt already showed the same lever from the other side (0.85 take-up moved this row from -0.0 to -52.4 percent). This PR gates the draw to units with an adult under State Pension age; the SPI-channel tenure defect is a #840/#145 item; the OBR line also carries supported and temporary accommodation the frame has no concept for. Re-measured on every evaluation with the three Housing Benefit caseload rows; renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair. Re-measured on arm 2 of the next policyengine-uk bump (policyengine-uk 2.151.0): still outside the 25 percent bound at design weights, and short at its calibrated weights, unbound. The row rests in part on households of the SPI support channel, so no new figure is given (SN 9422).
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (the 2026-09-16 status comment, issuecomment-5694598278, whose next-steps list this repair works, and the repairs plan María approved on 2026-09-16 with her population ruling on the U8 take-up entry; approver as author per the register convention). Expiry 2026-12-08 aligns the whole UC-repair tranche with the zero-band clock already on the register (microcosm#877), so the next spine re-adjudicates them together. Receipts: experiments/882-uc-repairs-receipts.md (R1 and R5, tools/diagnose_uk_legacy_benefits.py on spine-q, the Q50f candidate, FRS 2024-25 and the twins). Measured at its FY2024-25 period on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py, where any move from that gap is weight drift; rebind when the engine's duty on published clearances reproduces the receipts.

exclusions.name: obr.betting_and_gaming_duties
exclusions.reason: An identity, not a check: the lcfs_consumption stage levels each gambling base to HMRC's FY2024-25 cash receipts for its duty, or Machine Games Duty's liabilities for its band, over the engine's own rate (Gaming Duty's over the engine's effective-rate proxy, itself those receipts over the Gambling Commission's casino yield), at prior weights (microcosm#1359), so the engine charges the receipts back by construction: £3.619bn against OBR's £3.616bn in cash (+0.1 percent), the gap being Machine Games Duty's £612.3m of liabilities against its £609.2m of receipts. Only weight drift can move it, so the row is measured for drift and is no evidence that the gambling inputs are right: their test is who carries them, by income decile. Binding it would move weight onto the households that gamble to hold a level the build already sets. Measured at its FY2024-25 period on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; rebind if the bases come from published stakes or yield rather than receipts.

The national solve measures a declared period only on a stored column or a CGT dated measure, and this row's value is the engine's 2024 duty, so the first PR C national refused at the national problem. Binding it needs a dated duty measure, or bases bound at the frame's period. Until then the row is measured on every evaluation, beside the other excise rows.

With petrol plus diesel levelled to ONS 07.2.2 by the lcfs_consumption stage, the engine's 2025 fuel_duty read -9.9 percent against the row on its RAC price divisors (-8.1 percent on DESNZ's; policyengine-uk#2169 A), measured with the stage levelled to the June edition's 07.2.2 (the September edition's 2024 figure is 4.2 percent lower, GBP 35.460bn against GBP 37.025bn, so the next national re-measures it; Vahid's review of microcosm#1420). Binding it would pull weight toward fuel buyers to cover business use the household frame does not hold. Before the level step it read -34.5 percent at design weights and -17.7 percent calibrated on microcosm#1121's head, where the weights raised petrol 21 and diesel 34 percent from design to final. On the 2026-09-30 national problem the calibration with the four consumption-tax rows bound left petrol 18 and diesel 36 percent above a re-solve with the four consumption-tax rows masked together, in which the other 1,086 rows fitted no worse. Household road fuel is bound as ons.household_road_fuel_expenditure. Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; rebind if Microcosm comes to model business use of cars, which microcosm#1095 tracks.

exclusions.name: ons.household_gas_expenditure
exclusions.reason: Held out while ONS Consumer Trends 04.5.2 counts bottled gas (COICOP 04.5.2.2, liquefied hydrocarbons), which the frame holds in liquid_fuel_consumption (LCFS c45222), not in this mains-gas column. ONS's CPI weights put the sub-class at 2.2% (2024) to 3.2% (2026) of the class, so binding the whole class on mains gas would count bottled gas twice (Anthony's re-review of microcosm#1420, finding 2). The lcfs_consumption stage levels gas to DESNZ Energy Trends' domestic volume over calendar 2024 instead, and the local DESNZ gas rows bind at that level. microcosm#1095 tracks netting bottled gas out of the class once Chronicle carries the split. The row rebinds only with gas in the stage's spend_level_fuels as well: bound on a frame levelled to Energy Trends, it would pull the weights onto ONS's level, the pull microcosm#1113 took out (D1), and test_uk_energy_pricing.py holds the two together (the independent review of microcosm#1420, finding 11).
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-29 on microcosm#1420: hold the 04.5.2 target out and level gas on DESNZ until Chronicle carries bottled gas's share of the class.

exclusions.name: obr.ni_employer
exclusions.reason: Engine and period basis for roughly half of the gap; the rest is under investigation. policyengine-uk's ni_employer is the secondary Class 1 charge on each earner's pay above the secondary threshold, gross of the Employment Allowance, which employers offset against their secondary Class 1 liability through payroll, so OBR's receipts are net of it: HMRC's tax relief statistics (January 2026) put its cost at GBP 7.4bn for 2025-26 (a forecast), after the allowance rose to GBP 10,500 per employer and the GBP 100,000 eligibility restriction was removed from 6 April 2025. The row also binds the calendar-2025 window of the OBR fiscal years (three twelfths of FY2024-25, nine twelfths of FY2025-26), while the engine's 2025 period applies the FY2025-26 rules (the 15 percent rate and the GBP 5,000 secondary threshold) to the whole window, so its first quarter is overstated. On the K=15 local candidates measured for microcosm#1301 the row read about 20 percent above its target: the allowance accounts for about a quarter of that excess, the window for about a fifth and the under-21 zero rate, which the engine also omits, for under a tenth, so the stated parts explain roughly half of it. The rest sits in the pay level and may be a conflict between the bound pay targets and OBR's NICs base rather than a weighting defect. Bound, the row pulls pay down against those pay targets to close a gap at least half of which the weights did not open. Held out of the objective as a diagnostic and never fitted; rebind when a locked policyengine-uk nets the allowance out of ni_employer and the window takes each fiscal year's own rules.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-16 on the microcosm#1301 local release plan: unbind the row as a measured diagnostic, rather than bind the FY2025-26 value or sign it gate-only, because modelling the allowance alone would close only part of the gap. The exclusion applies on both lines, since this register has no line scoping: the national objective drops the row too, and a national run given a frozen scoring register derived before this entry fails closed (the re-derived register differs from the frozen one), so the national build's frozen register is derived from a head that carries this entry. policyengine-uk#2459, split from policyengine-uk#1918 (which keeps the under-21 and apprentice zero rates), asks the engine to net the allowance out of ni_employer. The expiry gives the three-month window of the 2026-10-08 engine-factor diagnostic (obr.vat).

exclusions.name: orr.rail_government_support
exclusions.reason: Measured on ORR table 7271's net operational government support from all sources, María's basis ruling of 2026-10-25 (microcosm#890 G, microcosm#736): table 7270's broad total adds enhancements and miscellaneous support, which are investment, not a subsidy any household's rail use carries. The frame's household rail subsidy (rail_subsidy_spending, the engine's rail_usage times gov.dft.rail.fare_index) sits below the row at design weights. Arm 2c of the policyengine-uk 2.151.0 bump (calibrate-only on arm 2's spine) bound it on table 7271: the row reached its target, but the weights concentrated past the release bound (uk_weight_ratio failed) and the effective sample size fell by about a tenth. So it stays held out of the objective as a measured diagnostic and is never fitted; rebind when the frame's rail use can reach it without that concentration.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-20 on the pre-Budget PR (microcosm#1278): hold the row out only if a national arm with it held out, run beside the calibration-period fix's arm (microcosm#1324), passes the gates and keeps the share of rows within 10 percent; otherwise keep it bound and label the distributional tables. The expiry, 2026-12-11, matches the uprating holds' renewal, after the Budget. Re-measured on 2026-10-24 on arm 2c of the policyengine-uk 2.151.0 bump: bound on table 7271 the row fails the weight-ratio gate. Her ruling of 2026-10-25 closed the basis question on table 7271 and kept the row held.

exclusions.name: slc.repayments.scotland_total
exclusions.reason: Model basis, not a weight question: Scotland's borrowers repay on Scotland's own plan thresholds (Plan 4 in Scotland, Plan 1 in Northern Ireland), but this build does not impute those plans for them (plan_4_imputation is False, and policyengine-uk#2636, the plan relabel issue, closed as not planned), so the engine reads English thresholds. Binding the row would reweight borrowers to cover a threshold gap. Measured on every evaluation as a diagnostic; rebind once the plans are modelled.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-29 on the plan for the next #1095 PR (microcosm#1095, item R4): bind Wales's SLC repayments, and hold Scotland's and Northern Ireland's until their plan thresholds are modelled for their borrowers.
